headline: Low interaction risk: no shared channel or write overlap is documented, but pdf.js can process PDFs while the other profile is an unverified docs-only NLP list.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared communication channel is documented. agent_a is an unverified docs-only awesome-nlp list with network_egress none, and agent_b is pdf.js with browser-based tests and PDF-file IO only. Without a bridge such as shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP, prompt injection between them is not plausible from the profiles alone.
conditions: IF a shared filesystem, clipboard, or MCP bridge is added between the agents, reassess injection risk.
IF agent_b begins parsing agent_a-produced text as instructions, the risk changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces.
Do not copy agent_a output into agent_b prompts automatically.
Disable any shared clipboard or message queue between them.

B_data_leakage.rationale: agent_a reports network_egress none and no data classes touched; agent_b also reports network_egress none and only PDF documents. There is no documented shared workspace or authenticated principal, so a leakage path is not evidenced. The pairwise interaction is undocumented, so uncertainty remains but does not justify a higher severity.
conditions: IF either agent is connected to a shared workspace containing sensitive files, reassess leakage.
IF either agent is configured to upload file contents to a backend, reassess leakage.
mitigations: Keep sensitive PDFs out of any shared directory.
Run both agents with separate OS users.
Verify no automatic file upload is enabled.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: No overlapping write capability is documented. agent_a has no IO surfaces or runnable surface shown, while agent_b exposes PDF-file IO and supports multiple instances but no filesystem write, git, db, or OAuth scopes. Because the profiles do not show a shared mutable resource, capability conflict is provably absent from the available evidence.
conditions: IF both agents are later granted write access to the same directory, reassess conflict.
IF either agent gains git or database write permissions, reassess conflict.
mitigations: Avoid granting write permissions to shared paths.
Document any future mutable resource ownership.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A cascading-error path is weakly possible only if agent_b treats agent_a output as authoritative. agent_a is a docs-only NLP list with no runnable surface, and agent_b is a PDF processor with browser-based tests; neither profile shows downstream action authority. Because the interaction is undocumented and no default trust chain is shown, the blast radius appears small.
conditions: IF agent_b is configured to ingest agent_a output without verification, reassess to medium.
IF agent_b is given authority to send emails, commit changes, or file tickets based on agent_a output, reassess upward.
mitigations: Add a verification step before using agent_a output.
Require human review for any downstream action.
Log provenance for any text passed from agent_a to agent_b.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data flow is documented. agent_b touches PDF documents, but agent_a lists no data classes touched and no residency, certification, or retention mismatch is shown for either agent. Since the profiles do not establish a regulated-data pathway, a compliance breach is not evidenced.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into the pair, reassess compliance.
IF either agent is deployed under conflicting retention or residency policies, reassess compliance.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair until policies are confirmed.
Record retention settings for both agents.
